title: Taser didn't cause Edmonton man's death: fatality report
article: A 33-year-old Edmonton man who died Christmas Eve 2005 after police used a Taser on him was killed by a cocaine overdose, not the shock device, according to a provincial fatality report released Thursday.
"Current medical research shows Tasering does not cause death," Provincial Court Judge Fred Day wrote of the evidence he heard during a five-day hearing in October.

Alessandro Fiacco was seen yelling and screaming in the middle of the road in a south-side neighbourhod, complaining of snakes and bees on his skin. Police used a Taser on him three times in an attempt to subdue him. In the ambulance on the way to hospital, he went into cardiac arrest and died.
Toxicology reports showed Fiacco had cocaine in his system that was five times the level normally considered life-threatening.
"There is an ever increasing body of anecdotal evidence about 'death due to Tasers,'" Day wrote in his report. But those reports show a "casual" rather than "causal" connection, he concluded.
The report makes no recommendations for changes in policy, although it does note the Alberta Solicitor General recently issued new provincial guidelines on the use of the stun devices.
